cards.explanation: The answer is gold, friends. Daniel 3:1 says King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue. Picture a whole statue of shiny gold standing out on that plain, and I'm over here getting excited about a gold base.
The answer is sixty cubits high, friends. Daniel 3:1 says the statue was sixty cubits high and six cubits wide. That is a tall, skinny statue, and nobody is getting a hat on that thing.

The answer is to attend the statue's dedication, friends. Daniel 3:2 says the king sent word to gather all those officials to attend the dedication of the statue he had set up. Think of it as a ribbon cutting, except the statue is the guest of honor.

The answer is to fall down and worship the statue, friends. Daniel 3:5 says that when they hear the music, they "…must fall down and worship the golden statue…" the king set up. The music was the cue, and the cue was a full band. The list runs from the horn and flute all the way to the pipes and all kinds of music.

The answer is the furnace, friends. Daniel 3:6 says whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace. The herald proclaimed it loudly, too. I know a thing or two about hot ovens, and I would not want to stand near that one.

The answer is True, friends. Daniel 3:7 says that as soon as they heard the music, the people of every nation and language would fall down and worship the golden statue. Everyone went down on cue, every nation and every language. I bet that was something to see, a whole crowd going down at once.
The answer is King Nebuchadnezzar, friends. In Daniel 3:12 the astrologers say these are Jews the king appointed to manage the province of Babylon. They basically told on someone he had hired.

The answer is False, friends. Even furious, the king spoke to them first. In Daniel 3:14 he asks if it is true that they do not serve his gods or worship the statue. Then comes more talking, in verse 15.

The answer is another chance to bow when the music plays, friends. Daniel 3:15 says that when they hear the music, if they are ready to fall down and worship the statue, "very good." He gave them a second try, and then he warned them about the furnace.

The answer is that He can deliver them from the furnace and the king's hand, friends. In Daniel 3:17 they say, "If the God whom we serve exists, then He is able to deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace and from your hand, O king." They name both the furnace and the king, and they say it right to his face.

The answer is False, and what a line it is, friends. Daniel 3:18 says, "But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden statue you have set up." They stay put whichever way it goes.

The answer is seven, friends. Daniel 3:19 says he gave orders to heat the furnace seven times hotter than usual. It was Nebuchadnezzar who gave that order. I burn a batch at the regular heat and I'm still sorry about it for days.

The answer is that the flames kill them, friends, and it's a heavy part. Daniel 3:22 says the king's command was so urgent and the furnace so hot that the flames killed the men who carried the three up. That tells us how hot it really was.

The answer is four men walking around unharmed, friends. Four, not three. In Daniel 3:25 the king says, "I see four men, unbound and unharmed, walking around in the fire…" They went in firmly bound and now nothing is tying anybody up.

The answer is servants of the Most High God, friends. In Daniel 3:26 the king calls out, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out!" Quite a change from the guy who was furious with rage a few verses back.

The answer is False, friends. Daniel 3:27 says the fire had no effect on their bodies, and there was no smell of fire on them. Not a hair of their heads was singed, either. They came out of a furnace seven times hotter than usual and didn't smell like it.

The answer is His angel, friends. In Daniel 3:28 Nebuchadnezzar says, "Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who has sent His angel and delivered His servants who trusted in Him." Those are the king's own words.

The answer is True, friends. In Daniel 3:29 the king decrees that anyone of any nation or language who says anything offensive against the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego will be cut into pieces. The decree also says their houses would be reduced to rubble. It's a harsh decree, and it's what the text says.

The answer is promoted, friends. Daniel 3:30 says the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the province of Babylon. It's the same province they were already managing. They went from the furnace to a better job.
